EARN ON YOUR BIGGEST SHOP

Not sure why but the past 3 months the offers have been almost one after the other and I shop at Woolies every week and use the rewards card.
--

I don't shop at Woolies due to the points, I like the brands and Coles refuses to sell them eg Mainland cheese, Ecostore Laundry Powder, the shampoo I buy, odd shaped apples for really cheap prices, the family pie brand etc etc. I went to our local Coles a while ago and they had like 2 brands of a cleaning product and one was their own brand. [User #1497315400 postsbananas_ozWhirlpool Forums Addict] TechnoLoGy writes...
How come mine was 2 x not 5 x !
Simple. You scan your card too much. The whole system works on getting people back to the shop, not rewarding people who already do.
This system works the same as insurance or broadband plans. New customers get better prices then existing ones.

[User #414352978 posts• MarƒoX •A boy trapped in a mans bodyWhirlpool Forums Addict] -Robbo- writes...
average shop per week is always over $180
Perhaps this is why ... You always spend significant sums regularly so no need to get you to spend.
We used to spend 200+ at WW until they abolished the previous card, so we went to Coles & spent nothing at WW.
After 12 months or more, we suddenly got an email offer (which co-incided with WW pushing to get back in the hunt against Coles) which was very generous (2 weeks x $100 to get points worth 11.25% discount). But the next one was cut back (2 weeks x $135 to get points worth only 7.4% discount). For us, the Coles ones were better ( 4 weeks x $120 to get points worth 10.4% discount) but those offers are few & far between lately.
